headline: Record underwriting profit drives sharp earnings growth
summary_short: American Financial Group reported Q2 2026 net earnings of $248M ($2.99/share), up 42.5% y/y, on record P&C pretax operating income of $350M and a 91.5% combined ratio, with revenue of $2,030M (+5.2% y/y).
summary_long: Revenue was $2,030M, up 5.2% y/y (+9.5% q/q), driven by 23% y/y growth in net investment income (mostly higher alternative-investment yields; P&C investment income ex-alternatives was flat) plus premium growth. Net earnings of $248M (EPS $2.99) rose 42.5% y/y on higher underwriting profit and alternative-investment returns; core operating earnings were $234M ($2.82/share, core ROE 19.2% ex-AOCI). P&C combined ratio improved to 91.5% from 93.1%. AFG repurchased $26M of stock and paid $0.88/share in dividends. Shareholders' equity rose 6.8% y/y to $4,821M despite a $142M AOCI drag. AFG expects to book a ~$125M pretax gain in Q3 2026 on the pending Charleston Harbor Resort & Marina sale.

drivers.explanation: Co-CEOs cite record P&C pretax operating income, healthy premium growth, and strong underwriting margins as driving the quarter; core operating ROE reached 19.2%, up from 15.5% a year ago.

Net investment income rose 23% y/y on higher alternative-investment yields (P&C investment income ex-alternatives was flat); net earned premiums and 6% growth in net written premiums also contributed.
Record P&C pretax operating income of $350M (vs $273M) reflects higher underwriting profit and a jump in alternative-investment income to $50M pretax from $8M a year ago.

Core net operating earnings rose on higher underwriting profit and stronger alternative-investment returns; net earnings also carried $14M of non-core realized gains versus a $5M non-core loss a year ago.
Follows the net-income drivers above; diluted share count fell slightly (-0.6% y/y) after $26M of buybacks this quarter, a modest arithmetic lift to per-share earnings.
Book value per share rose 4.8% including dividends this quarter, per the release, driven by earnings growth partly offset by a $142M swing in AOCI on unrealized bond marks.
Not explained in the release — no discussion of debt issuance or refinancing accompanies this balance.
